description: A full-window view over the chat that lays a kubeconfig cluster out as Freelens does: a top bar to pick the cluster context, namespaces and a filter, a sidebar of resource categories under Home (the whole stack's CPU and memory), a table of the chosen kind's objects with Freelens' columns, the selected object's YAML beside it, and pods' followed logs and shells in them under both, a tab each. Read-only except for pod deletes, each asked first, and what's typed in a pod's shell. It reads the clusters of the host picked in the window's host dropdown, through that host's host process, and can move out to a window of its own and back.
opens: A running workload in a Signal link's popover (Running section): opens its context, on its kind's page, filtered to its name, in its namespace
A Kubernetes cluster's icon button in a Signal link's popover (Open this cluster in the Kubernetes view): opens that context
⌘K / Ctrl+K glossary: a running workload or a cluster context

parts.name: top bar
parts.shows: A bar as tall as a header bar (on macOS with room at the left for the window's traffic lights). From left: the title, the host's name, a context picker, a namespaces button, a filter box, a gap, a refresh button, Move to Its Own Window, a close button. Dragging it moves the window; double-clicking it maximizes.

parts.name: title
parts.shows: Heading "Kubernetes"

parts.name: host
parts.shows: The host the view reads, by name, dim (as ☰ → Terminal's bar names its terminal's host): the one picked in the window's host dropdown when the view opened, this machine's when none is.

parts.name: context picker
parts.shows: A drop-down of every kubeconfig context (clusters no context names are not listed). Shows the picked context's name, truncated in the middle past about 32 characters. The one used last is picked on open, else the kubeconfig's current one, else the first. No "(current)" suffix.

actions.does: Switches to that cluster: the table fades, the logs close and their kubectl stops, the YAML closes, any watch stops, then the cluster's resources, namespaces and node count are read and the page is read again. Each context remembers the namespaces shown in it; the context is remembered across sessions.

parts.name: namespaces button
parts.shows: A button with a down arrow showing which namespaces are shown: "All namespaces", the one name, two names joined by a comma, or "3 namespaces" (n namespaces) from three up. Its tooltip is "Namespaces shown (any of them at once)", or, with more than two chosen, the full comma-joined list of names. With none chosen it reads "0 namespaces".

actions.does: Opens a popover: an "All namespaces" check, a separator, then a scrolling list (up to about 420 px tall) of a check per namespace of the cluster, sorted by name (plus any shown namespace the cluster didn't list, such as one opened from a link).
While every namespace is shown (it and every namespace checked): unchecks them all, and no namespace's objects are shown. Otherwise: checks every namespace and shows every namespace's objects.

Adds it to or removes it from the set shown, in the order picked; the table fades and is filtered (nothing is read again). Any number can be on at once. Unticking one while all are shown shows all the rest; every one ticked is All namespaces (ticked too); none ticked shows no namespace's objects. Every namespace is ticked while All namespaces is (GroupByMenu.menu.json's decision of 2026-11-26).

parts.name: filter
parts.shows: A search box, placeholder "Filter", about 22 characters wide, tooltip "Filter (Ctrl+F)". Rows are kept if any cell's text contains the typed text (any case); the matching text is highlighted in the cells.

actions.does: Filters the table live (no reading again), and the status line's count updates.
Clears the text if there is some; otherwise closes the view (see Esc below).

actions.by: key Ctrl+F (⌘F on macOS) while the view is open
actions.does: Focuses the filter with its text selected to type over. In the YAML or logs, their own Ctrl+F finds in them instead.

parts.name: refresh
parts.shows: A refresh icon button, tooltip "Read it again"; it spins while a read is going on.

actions.does: Reads the page again (the table fades while it does).

parts.name: Move to Its Own Window
parts.shows: A flat window icon button, tooltip "Move to Its Own Window". Hidden while the view is out.

actions.does: The view moves to a window of its own titled as its heading, all of it as it was (its context, its watch, its dock's tabs); the window under it is left showing what the view covered. The view's bar becomes that window's header bar: its controls sit in the window's title bar beside the window's own controls (on macOS its traffic lights), with no band above the view; there the bar leaves out Move to Its Own Window, its × and the traffic lights' room, as the window has its own. Back over the window it came from, the bar is as it was. Opening the view again brings that window up, as it is: nothing is read again (the tabs, the watch and the diagram go on) unless another host is picked. Closing that window puts the view back over the window it came from, shown. Closing the window it came from closes it too.

decisions.said: Kubernetes and the Database viewer can detach to a window of their own, as Emission does
decisions.rule: Every desktop app's Kubernetes and database views have Move to Its Own Window in their bar: the same view, still reading, moves to a window of its own; closing that window puts it back over the window it came from

decisions.said: The Kubernetes view out in its own window should use the window's top bar, not leave a band of empty space at the top (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: In every app, a view moved out to a window of its own (Kubernetes, Database Schemas, and any view built the same way) puts its bar's controls in that window's title bar or header bar, with nothing empty above the view; back over the window it came from, its bar is as it was

parts.name: close
parts.shows: A round × button, tooltip "Close (Esc)". Hidden while the view is out (its window has its own close).

actions.does: Closes the view: the logs' kubectl is stopped, any watch and the refresh timer stop, and the chat's input box gets the focus back.

parts.name: sidebar of categories
parts.shows: A left column about 230 px wide (scrolls vertically) listing Freelens' categories. A category with several kinds is a heading row (the category's icon, its name, and a down arrow, or a right arrow when folded) with its kinds nested under it, indented to line up with the heading's name. A category of one kind is just that kind's row carrying the category's icon (Nodes, Namespaces, Events). One row is selected: the page shown. Home is the page on first open (a link that opens the view on a kind opens on that kind). A kind this cluster doesn't serve is dimmed and can't be picked; its tooltip is "<context> doesn't serve <kind>". Categories and kinds, in order: Home (its own row, a house icon, first); Nodes (shown only when the cluster has more than one node, or when it's the page shown); Workloads: Pods, Deployments, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, ReplicaSets, Replication Controllers, Jobs, CronJobs, Rollouts (Argo, only where installed); Config: ConfigMaps, Secrets, Resource Quotas, Limit Ranges, Horizontal Pod Autoscalers, Vertical Pod Autoscalers, Pod Disruption Budgets, Priority Classes, Runtime Classes, Leases, Mutating Webhook Configurations, Validating Webhook Configurations, Validating Admission Policies, Validating Admission Policy Bindings; KEDA (only on a cluster with KEDA): Scaled Objects, Scaled Jobs, Trigger Authentications, Cluster Trigger Authentications; Network: Services, Endpoints, Endpoint Slices, Ingresses, Ingress Classes, Network Policies, HTTP Routes (Gateway API), Ingress Routes (Traefik), Virtual Services (Istio); Storage: Persistent Volume Claims, Persistent Volumes, Storage Classes; Namespaces; Events; Helm: Releases; User Management: Service Accounts, Cluster Roles, Roles, Cluster Role Bindings, Role Bindings; Certificates (cert-manager, only where installed): Certificates, Issuers, Cluster Issuers; Monitoring (Prometheus Operator, only where installed): Service Monitors, Pod Monitors, Prometheus Rules; Custom Resources: Definitions. The optional custom-resource kinds' rows, and a category's heading when none of its kinds is served, are not listed at all on a cluster that lacks them (rather than dimmed).

actions.does: Shows that kind's page: the YAML closes and the table is read again (the logs stay).
Folds its kinds away, or shows them again; which categories are folded is remembered across sessions.

phone.does: A page of its own, the bar's ◂ from the table. A category's heading is the body's size, bold (the desktop's 0.85em), its row at least 30 high; a kind's row at least 23 high (the desktop's 26)
phone.why: The owner: on the phone the categories' headings should be a bit bigger and their rows a bit narrower

decisions.said: On the phone, the category headings should be a bit bigger and the rows under them a bit narrower (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app draws a category's heading row bolder and taller than the kind rows under it, its name at the body's size, and keeps the kind rows compact

parts.name: Home
parts.shows: In the table's place while Home is picked (the YAML pane and the dock as ever), scrolling: two cards side by side (one above the other where there isn't room), CPU then Memory, each with a rule round it and rounded corners. A card's head: its name (bold) and, at the right, dim, what every node can give pods together (their allocatable: "4 cores", "7.7GiB"; tooltip "What the nodes can give pods (their allocatable)"). Under it three rows, Requested, Used and Limits: the word (its tooltip says what it adds up), a bar 10 px tall with round ends filled to the amount's share of allocatable (Requested in the accent, Used green, Limits grey; any of them past allocatable full and orange), the amount (CPU in cores to two places, "1.10"; memory as the table's, "704.0MiB"; "N/A" for Used without a metrics API; "–" for Limits when no container sets one) and its share ("27%") dim. No bars when the nodes can't be listed. Under the rows, how it went: Used as a green line and Requested as a dashed line in the accent, over the history the host keeps (tooltip "Used (and requested, dashed) over the last 30 minutes"), each sample at its time across the 30 minutes up to the newest, so a stretch with none (the host off, the cluster unreachable) is a gap in the lines; scaled to the most either reached; nothing drawn with fewer than two samples. Under the cards a table of the namespaces shown, a row each, sorted by name: Namespace, Pods, CPU requested, CPU used, CPU limits, Memory requested, Memory used, Memory limits, its head dim and bold, numbers to the right. On a cluster of more than one node (as the Nodes row), a table of the nodes under it: Node, Pods, CPU requested, CPU used, CPU limits, CPU allocatable, Memory requested, Memory used, Memory limits, Memory allocatable; pods not yet on a node are a row of their own, "Unscheduled", with no allocatable. Each 10 s read changes the tables' texts in place (a row added or gone, or new columns, lays them out anew). The filter keeps the rows any cell of which has its text. The tables scroll sideways when they're wider than the room. The host adds it up (kube's summary; schema/types KubeSummary): every app asks and draws its answer (schema/ui README: apps are thin clients). A read under the Kubernetes read rule, as list is. Requested and limits are the pods' that hold on to their node (not Succeeded or Failed ones), each pod's as the scheduler reckons it (the sidecar KEP's order): its containers' and sidecars' summed, or, if more, the most any init container needs while it runs beside the sidecars started before it; plus its overhead (a request's always, a limit's only where a limit is set); a limit is the sum of those set, as kubectl describe node adds them. The host reads only what that needs: kubectl get pods with a field selector leaving out Succeeded and Failed ones, -o jsonpath of each pod's namespace, name, node and overhead and its containers' and init containers' resources and restartPolicy. Used is the metrics API's pods (metrics-server) summed, so it adds up with the namespaces' and nodes' rows; without one it's N/A and the status line says so. Allocatable is every node's status.allocatable summed; a node's row is against its own. History: from the first time Home is read for a context, the host samples it every 10 s until its process ends, whether Home is open or not (only contexts Home has been read for; one not read for a day is let go), each namespace's requested and used, for 30 minutes, in its own memory (none kept on disk; a host restarted starts again); the totals of the namespaces shown are worked out from them. An app asks only for the samples after the newest it has (since) and keeps the last 30 minutes'.

actions.does: The totals, the history and the namespaces table are those namespaces' (the host adds them up again); allocatable stays every node's.

actions.by: click a namespace's name (a link, tooltip "Only <namespace>'s")
actions.does: Shows only that namespace, as a namespace link in a table does.
Read again every 10 s, as a list that isn't watched is; Refresh reads it at once.

decisions.said: A home page that records the total memory and CPU requests, usage and limits used by the whole stack (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Kubernetes view opens on Home, the first row of its sidebar: the stack's CPU and memory requested, used and limits, each against what the nodes can give pods, with a short history, by namespace and by node, as the host adds them up

decisions.said: Keep sampling a context every 10 s from the first time Home is read for it until the host process exits, whether or not Home is open; sample only clusters the user has opened on Home (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every host samples Home's totals for each context Home has been read for every 10 s, open or not, and every app plots the samples by their time so a stretch without any shows as a gap

parts.name: table
parts.shows: A scrolling table of the page's objects, one row per object, with Freelens' columns for the kind, no row or column separators. Columns can be resized; Name is about 220 px and Namespace about 120 px wide by default, Name expands to fill, and the table scrolls sideways when it's wider than the room. A cell's text is cut with … and carries a tooltip of the full text when it is long (over about 30 characters for a Name, 40 otherwise). Age cells show how old (45s, 3m05s under ten minutes, 42m, 5h07m under a day, then 3d), and their tooltip is the full creation time. Status cells are coloured by tone: green (Running, Succeeded, Active, Bound, Available, Complete, Ready, Deployed, True, Normal), orange (Pending, Terminating, Finalizing, Waiting, ContainerCreating, Released, Suspended and similar), red (Failed, Evicted, Error, NotReady, Lost, Warning, Unknown, and anything with BackOff, err or OOM in it, such as CrashLoopBackOff), plain otherwise; for a multi-part status the first part sets the colour. Sorting: click a column heading to sort by it, again to reverse; numbers, ages and sizes sort by value, text as text. Rows start sorted by Name (Events: by Last Seen). The selected row is highlighted. Columns per kind: Pods: Name, Namespace, Containers, CPU, Memory, Restarts, Controlled By, Node (only on a cluster of more than one node), Age, Status, then a last unlabelled column with the row buttons. Nodes: Name, CPU, Memory, Roles, Version, Internal IP, Age, Conditions. Deployments: Name, Namespace, Ready (ready/desired), Desired, Updated, Available, Age, Conditions. DaemonSets: Name, Namespace, Desired, Current, Ready, Updated, Available, Node Selector, Age. StatefulSets: Name, Namespace, Ready, Desired, Age. ReplicaSets and Replication Controllers: Name, Namespace, Desired, Current, Ready, Age. Jobs: Name, Namespace, Status, Succeeded, Completions, Parallelism, Duration, Age. CronJobs: Name, Namespace, Schedule, Timezone, Suspended (Yes/No), Active, Last schedule, Age. ConfigMaps: Name, Namespace, Keys, Age. Secrets: Name, Namespace, Keys, Type, Age. Services: Name, Namespace, Type, Cluster IP, External IP, Ports, Age, Status. Ingresses: Name, Namespace, LoadBalancers, Rules, Age. Persistent Volume Claims: Name, Namespace, Storage class, Size, Age, Status. Persistent Volumes: Name, Storage Class, Capacity, Claim, Age, Status. Namespaces: Name, Labels, Age, Status. Events: Type, Message, Namespace, Involved Object, Source, Count, Age, Last Seen. Helm Releases: Name, Namespace, Chart, Revision, App Version, Status, Updated. Custom Resource Definitions: Resource, Group, Version, Scope, Age. Other kinds (Config's, Network's, Storage's, User Management's, KEDA, cert-manager, monitoring) have the same shape: Name, Namespace (if namespaced), their own few columns, Age. A custom resource opened from a definition shows the printer columns its definition declares.

parts.name: namespace cell (a link)
parts.shows: In a Namespace column, the namespace's name as a flat link-looking button; tooltip "Only <namespace>'s"

actions.does: Shows only that namespace's objects (the namespaces shown become just it).

parts.name: controlled-by cell (a link)
parts.shows: In a pod's Controlled By column, the owner as "Kind/name" as a link-looking button

actions.does: Status line says "Finding <kind>/<name>…"; climbs ReplicaSet to its Deployment and Job to its CronJob (up to three steps), then goes to that kind's page with that object selected and scrolled into view (its YAML opens beside the table). The filter is cleared, and the owner's namespace is added to the namespaces shown if it wasn't one of them. If the owner isn't in the list the status line says "<owner> isn't in <kinds> on <context>"; if the kind has no page here, "<kind>/<name>: no page here for <kind>".

parts.name: containers cell (squares)
parts.shows: In the Pods table's Containers column, a small rounded square (10 px, 3 px apart) per container, init containers first: solid green (running and ready), solid orange (waiting, starting or running but not ready yet), green with an orange ring (ready, but its last run ended less than an hour ago: restarted lately), solid red (crashed, failed, an image that won't pull, exited with an error), faint grey (completed, exit 0: an init container's, a job's). Tooltip: one line per container, "name: state" (init ones "name (init)"), the state being words such as "running, ready", "running, not ready yet", "running, ready, restarted 12m ago, at <time>", "completed", "terminated: Error (exit code 1)", "terminated: <reason>", "waiting: CrashLoopBackOff", "waiting", "not started yet", each with " (1 restart)" or " (n restarts)" appended when it has restarted. The column sorts and filters by its ready/total count ("1/2").

phone.does: A long-press on a square shows its tooltip's words

parts.name: CPU and Memory cells
parts.shows: Pods and Nodes: CPU in cores to three decimals (0.012), Memory in B, KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB with one decimal (12.4MiB); "N/A" when the cluster has no metrics API.

parts.name: pod row buttons
parts.shows: At the end of each Pods row, three flat icon buttons: a logs button (tooltip "Logs"), a shell button (a terminal icon, tooltip "Shell") and a ⋮ menu button (tooltip "Delete…"). The column's heading is blank and not clickable.

actions.does: Opens the pod's logs pane under the table (see logs).
Opens a shell in the pod under the table (see shell pane).
Opens a menu of two items, Delete and Force delete (see pod menu).

parts.name: row selection
parts.shows: Nothing is selected to start with.

actions.does: Selects it and opens its YAML beside the table (see YAML).

actions.by: double-click or press Enter on a Namespaces row
actions.does: Shows only that namespace's pods: the page goes to Pods with the namespaces shown set to that one.

actions.by: double-click or press Enter on a Custom Resource Definitions row
actions.does: Adds a row for that definition's kind to the sidebar (under Definitions), selects it, and shows that kind's objects with the columns the definition declares.

parts.name: column filter
parts.shows: On a column whose values are words (not a name, age or containers column; one that sorts by its text, not a number, size or time; each value with a letter in it and at most 40 characters), with 30 or fewer different values and some value shared by more than one row (any number for a status column), hovering its heading shows a funnel button at the heading's right end. While the column filters, the funnel stays, in the accent. A value hidden but not in the list now stays hidden, listed with a count of 0; a value with a count of 0 is greyed (dim) but can still be ticked. A filter on a column the table doesn't show (the Node column on a cluster of one node) hides nothing until the column is back.

actions.by: click the funnel (the phone: hold the heading, or tap its funnel while it filters)
actions.does: Opens a popover: an "All" check, a separator, then a check per value of the column in the rows the other filters leave (and any value hidden), sorted by name, each "Value (n)" with how many rows have it; an empty cell is "(none)". The namespaces button's checklist.

Hides or shows the rows with that value at once (nothing is read again); remembered in the settings for the kind (kube_hidden, Docker's docker_hidden: {kind: {column title: [values hidden]}}). All ticks every value; unticking All hides every row.

decisions.said: WE should be able to hover over container status, click a filter button on the right aligned and then see a chckbox dropdown to filter by the set of strings i.e. I usually want to filter out Succeeded / Failed nad only see running jobs.
decisions.rule: Every app's resource tables (Kubernetes' kinds, Docker's pages) let a column of a few words be filtered by its values: a filter button at the column heading's right end (shown on hover, kept and in the accent while it filters; on a touch screen, holding the heading opens it and the funnel sits just after the title while it filters) opens All over a check per value with its row count; unticked values' rows are hidden, together with the namespaces picked and the filter box, and the status line counts the rows shown. The values hidden are remembered per kind (or Docker page) across refreshes and restarts, so hiding Succeeded and Failed pods stays.

decisions.said: UX -- in the filter column fileds with no elements should be slighlt grayed out but still clickavble
decisions.rule: In every app's column filter, a value no row has (a count of 0) is drawn greyed, as a dim label, and stays a check that can be ticked or unticked.

parts.name: YAML pane
parts.shows: Appears to the right of the table (at least 360 px wide, the table keeping about two thirds, with a draggable divider) once a row is selected. A header line: the object's title, "<Kind> <name>" plus " · <namespace>" when it has one (the kind is the page's title with a trailing s dropped; truncated in the middle), and a flat × button (tooltip "Hide"). Below it the object's YAML as read-only code: highlighted, with line numbers, the code zoom's size, Ctrl+F finding in it. Names of other objects inside it (an owner, a service, a secret, a node…) are underlined links; the text stays selectable. While the YAML is read again it goes grey until the new text is in, and if it is the same object read again it stays where it was scrolled to. A Secret shows only a comment header, "# Secret <ns>/<name> (<type>)", "# Its values aren't shown." and "keys:" with each key's name (its values are never read). A Helm release shows its listed fields as JSON. A read that fails shows one comment line "# <title>: <why>".

actions.does: Hides the pane and deselects the row.

actions.by: click a link in the YAML
actions.does: Goes to that object: its kind's page, it selected and scrolled to (same as the Controlled By click); a Namespace link shows only that namespace's objects.
Closes the shell or the logs first if open, else the YAML, else the whole view. In the shell, Esc goes to the program in it.

parts.name: pod menu
parts.shows: The ⋮ button's menu on a pod row: two items, "Delete" and "Force delete".

actions.does: Asks first in a dialog (see delete dialog); only the dialog's Delete button deletes.
Asks first in a stronger dialog (see delete dialog).

parts.name: delete dialog
parts.shows: A modal alert over the window. Heading "Delete pod <name>?" (or "Force delete pod <name>?"). Body paragraphs, in this order: "In namespace <ns>, on <context>."; for a cluster whose API server isn't on this machine, "This is a remote cluster: <context>'s API server isn't on this machine."; for a normal delete "Its containers are stopped, given their grace period to finish.", for a force delete "Force delete doesn't wait for the pod to stop: the cluster forgets it at once, while its containers may go on running on their node for a while."; then "It's controlled by <Kind> <name>, which may start another in its place." or "No controller owns it: nothing will start it again." Buttons: Cancel (default; also what Esc or closing does) and a destructive-styled "Delete" (force: "Force Delete").

actions.does: Status line says "Deleting pod <name>…" (force: "Force deleting pod <name>…"); kubectl runs off the main thread; then the status line says what kubectl said, else "pod "<name>" deleted", or "couldn't delete pod <name>: <why>"; the list is read again. The message stays first in the status line for 30 seconds through refreshes.
Nothing runs.

parts.name: dock
parts.shows: Docks under the table and the YAML, the width of both, with a draggable divider (opens at about half the height, at least 140 px tall; the table keeps the rest), while it has a tab. A strip on the frame, its grey (the bars' and the sidebar's), of a tab per pod's logs or shell in a pod, any number of each, in the order opened: each tab its icon (logs, or a terminal), "<pod> · <namespace>" (truncated in the middle) and a small round × (tooltip "Close"); the picked tab drawn in the inside's colour, its top corners rounded, joined to what's under it. The picked tab's controls at the strip's end; under the strip, inside, its log or terminal.

actions.does: Picks it: its log or terminal shown, its controls at the strip's end.

actions.by: click a tab's ×, or middle-click it
actions.does: Closes it and stops what it runs (kubectl; the shell in the pod), never left running; the tab beside it is picked. The last one closed hides the dock. Switching context, another host, closing the view or Esc (the picked tab) do the same.

phone.does: The picked tab's controls (its container, Previous, Follow, Wrap) sit on a row of their own just under the strip, inside the picked tab, above its log or terminal: a phone's width holds only the tabs
phone.why: no room at the strip's end on a phone

decisions.said: The pod-name row under the Kubernetes table should be the shell's grey, and tab-like, holding several log tails and terminals at once, as Freelens does
decisions.rule: Every app docks pods' logs and shells under the Kubernetes table as tabs on a strip in the frame's grey, any number at once; the picked tab is drawn in the inside's colour, joined to the log or terminal under it
On the phone the Kubernetes dock's controls sit under the tab strip, inside the picked tab; elsewhere at the strip's end

parts.name: logs tab
parts.shows: A pod's logs (its row's logs button; the pod's tab picked again if it has one). Its controls at the strip's end: a small dim state text ("following", "its previous run", "ended (its container stopped)", "kubectl exited with <code>", or "kubectl: <error>"), a container picker, then flat buttons: Previous (toggle), Follow (toggle, a down-to-bottom icon, on by default), Wrap (toggle, a wrap icon; remembered across sessions, every log's at once), Find (a find icon). Inside under the strip, the log as read-only code with line numbers (the same code view: highlighted by its language guess, Ctrl+F finds in it, code zoom applies). A log starts at the pod's last 500 lines and keeps the newest 20,000 as it follows (the oldest are dropped a tenth at a time).

parts.name: container picker
parts.shows: A drop-down (tooltip "Container") of the pod's containers, init containers first and marked "<name> (init)". Opens on the container named by the pod's kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container annotation, else its first non-init container.

actions.does: Stops the current kubectl and follows that container's log from the start (last 500 lines).

parts.name: Previous
parts.shows: A toggle button labelled "Previous", tooltip "Its previous run's log (one that crashed, say), instead of this one's". Off whenever a pod is opened.

actions.does: On: shows the container's previous run's log (not followed; the state text says "its previous run"). Off: this run's log, followed.

parts.name: Follow
parts.shows: A toggle button, tooltip "Follow: keep to the newest line (scrolling up stops it, scrolling to the end again goes on)". On while the log keeps to its newest line.

actions.does: On: jumps to the end and keeps to the newest line. Off: stays where scrolled.

actions.by: scroll up (wheel, scrollbar drag, or keys Up, Page Up, Home)
actions.does: Turns Follow off by itself.
Turns Follow on again by itself.

parts.name: Wrap
parts.shows: A toggle button, tooltip "Wrap long lines", remembered across sessions

actions.does: Wraps long lines at the pane's width, or scrolls sideways.

parts.name: Find
parts.shows: A flat find button, tooltip "Find (Ctrl+F)"

actions.does: Opens the find bar over the log (see CodeView: find bar).

parts.name: shell tab
parts.shows: A shell in a pod (its row's shell button; a new tab each time). Its controls at the strip's end: a small dim state text (empty while it runs, "kubectl exited with <code>" once it ends), a container picker of the pod's running containers (not init containers). Inside under the strip (without VTE in the app: the missing-dependency state, "Terminal needs VTE", its install command with Copy, and Restart), a Multiplex terminal running kubectl exec -it in the container (on the host the view reads, run there by its host process when that's another host, with the kubectl that host is set to use): bash if the container has it, else sh. Its text in the window's light or dark colours. Its edges glow in the accent while a Bot is at its terminal tools there, as Emission's page does.

actions.does: Ends the shell and starts one in that container.
Goes to the shell in the pod, as in any terminal.

parts.name: status line
parts.shows: A single dim line under the table, truncated at the end, of parts joined with " · ": a note first while it's fresh (a delete's result, an owner not found; 30 seconds), the count ("7 pods", or "3 pods of 7" when the filter or namespaces hide some), "In <namespaces>" folded into the count when namespaces are chosen ("3 pods of 7 in shop, jobs") and the metrics note ("CPU and memory from the metrics API, every 10 s", or "no metrics API on this cluster (CPU and memory N/A)"; Pods and Nodes only). The same line says progress: "Connecting to <context>…", "Reading <kinds> on <context>…", "Finding <kind>/<name>…", and, when a watch can't be kept, "can't watch <kinds> (<why>): read every <n> s instead". On Home: a fresh note, then the metrics note, nothing else.

decisions.said: "Read-only but for the deletes you confirm" / "<context name> (obvious from top bar)" / "live" not needd / "36 pods" fine
decisions.rule: Every app's Kubernetes status line is the count ("36 pods") and, for Pods and Nodes, the metrics note (after a fresh note, if any), and nothing else while it shows a list: no context name (the bar has it), no "live", no read-only note

parts.name: live updating
parts.shows: While the view is open the list is watched (kubectl get --watch) so rows appear, change and go as the cluster changes; where a watch isn't possible the list is read again every 10 s. Pods' and Nodes' CPU and memory are read again every 10 s. A row selected stays selected through a refresh (and its YAML stays unless the object's version changed). Home is read again every 10 s.

parts.name: keys
parts.shows: Esc closes in layers: the dock's picked tab, then the YAML, then the view (out in a window of its own: not the view) (a filter with text in it clears first). Ctrl+F focuses the filter. Ctrl +/−/0 and Ctrl+scroll over the YAML or logs change the code text size for every code view, not the chat's.

phone.why: Hardware-keyboard shortcuts; every action has a button too

actions.does: Closes the dock's picked tab, else the YAML, else the view.
Focuses the filter.

states.name: kubectl missing
states.shows: kubectl isn't on the host the view reads (as its host says, or this machine): the table is replaced by the missing-dependency state (schema/ui README: a missing dependency is shown one way): a package icon, "Kubernetes needs kubectl", the host's own install command with Copy, and Try Again, which clears the missing state first and then reads the host's contexts again (the table is back once kubectl is there). Nothing kubectl reads is read meanwhile; the status line is empty.

decisions.said: Think about guidance for installing what Baude depends on (claude, codex, vte3, kubectl, docker) and how Baude behaves when they aren't there (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Kubernetes view on a host without kubectl shows the missing-dependency state with that host's install command, never kubectl's own error

states.name: no kubeconfig context
states.shows: The table area is empty and the status line says "No kubeconfig context to show: <where>." where <where> is the kubeconfig path(s) (shortened with ~), or "~/.kube/config (there is none)" when no file is set up. Nothing is read.

states.name: connecting / reading
states.shows: The table fades (greys) while a context's resources are read and while a kind, a namespace-switching page or another read is loading; the refresh button spins. Background refreshes every 10 s do not fade it.

states.name: cluster can't be read
states.shows: The table is replaced by a centred message: a warning icon, a title, the reason (dim, selectable, centred), a copyable fix command in monospace with a copy button (tooltip "Copy"; copying toasts "Copied: run it in a terminal, then Try Again"), a "Try Again" pill button, and a folded "kubectl's output" expander holding all kubectl wrote (monospace, selectable; shown only when it differs from the reason). The status line says ": ". The kinds: "AWS profile <p> isn't set up", "AWS sign-in expired", "No valid AWS credentials", "Google Cloud sign-in expired", "Azure sign-in expired", "<program> isn't installed" with a reason that kubectl signs in with it and it isn't on Baude's PATH, "Signing in needs a terminal", "The cluster didn't accept your credentials", "Not allowed", "The cluster's certificate isn't trusted", "The cluster isn't running" (a local cluster) or "Can't reach the cluster", "Signing in with <program> failed", else "kubectl failed" with the last line kubectl wrote. The shown table's rows are cleared. Try Again reconnects from the start if the cluster never connected, else reads the page again.

states.name: kind not served
states.shows: A sidebar row is dimmed, not clickable, with the tooltip "<context> doesn't serve <kind>". If the page shown becomes unserved after a context switch, Pods is shown instead.

states.name: no containers to show logs of
states.shows: Clicking Logs on a pod with no containers shows no pane; the status line says "<pod> has no containers to show logs of".

states.name: logs ended
states.shows: The logs' state text reads "ended (its container stopped)" when kubectl ends cleanly, or "kubectl exited with <code>" when it fails. The log stays on screen.

states.name: single-node cluster
states.shows: No Nodes row in the sidebar and no Node column in Pods (every pod would say the same).

states.name: empty table
states.shows: The column headings with no rows; the status line counts "0 <kinds>".

states.name: another host
states.shows: The bar names the host picked; its contexts, its clusters' objects, YAML, logs and shells are read and run there by its host process. A host that can't be reached says "<host>: <why>" in the status line.

removed.name: The context's name, "live" and "read-only but for the deletes you confirm" in the status line
removed.why: The owner: "Read-only but for the deletes you confirm" / "<context name> (obvious from top bar)" / "live" not needd / "36 pods" fine

decisions.said: Kubernetes and Database Schemas should run on the host picked in the left pane, as Terminal does
decisions.rule: Every app's Kubernetes and database views read the clusters and databases of the host picked in the window's host picker (the host ☰ → Terminal opens new terminals on), through that host's host process, and their bar names that host
